# Decision points

Every decision point mu has, 40 in all, grouped as the desktop app's settings group them. Each is asked as a short question about a small state; [How mu works](../architecture.md) explains the engine and [Judges](../judges.md) who answers.

Each point has a mode:

- `active`: The verdict takes effect.
- `shadow`: Asked and logged, but changes nothing. Use it to see how well the judge does before relying on it.
- `off`: Not asked; this decision point is off.

Every point is `active` unless set otherwise (`"modes": { "default": "active" }` is the built-in default). `context.compact` and `output.drift` belong to features that are off by default, so they don't run until you turn those features on. Set `"default": "shadow"`, or a point's own mode, in `~/.mu/agent/mu.json` to only record verdicts; the desktop app's settings switch a point on or off; `/mu mode <point|default> <off|shadow|active>` switches one for the current session. See [Configuration](../configuration.md).

The feature column names the switch in `features` that turns the whole behavior off; its options are in [Features](features.md).

## Input

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input.preflight` | Message preflight | Classifies each message and how much thinking it needs, then gives the model a one-line hint; it can also set the turn's thinking level. | [`preflight`](features.md#preflight) |
| `task.frame` | Task frame update | Classifies each message as a new task, a new hard constraint, a correction, a new subgoal or no change. Only a change makes a model rewrite the task frame. | [`frame`](features.md#frame) |
| `input.interjection` | Mid-run messages | For a message that arrives while the agent is working: interrupt now, or handle it after the current step. | [`interjection`](features.md#interjection) |

## Context

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skills.disclosure` | Skill disclosure | Only skills relevant to the task go into the prompt; the rest stay hidden but findable. | [`skills`](features.md#skills) |
| `capability.disclosure` | Capability disclosure | Packs and MCP servers stay installed but hidden until a task needs them; their processes start only then. | [`catalog`](features.md#catalog) |
| `tool.admission` | Tool output admission | Judges long tool output in chunks; only what matters enters the context, and the rest is archived behind a pointer. | [`admission`](features.md#admission) |
| `tool.admission.test-log` | Test log trimming | Keeps one copy of exact repeats in test output; optionally, the judge picks what's needed from the rest. | [`admission`](features.md#admission) |
| `context.forget` | Forgetting stale results | When context use crosses a threshold, replaces stale tool results with one-line placeholders in outgoing requests. | [`forgetting`](features.md#forgetting) |
| `context.compact` | Summary-free compaction | When compacting, the judge keeps or prunes each passage instead of having a model write a summary. | [`compaction`](features.md#compaction) |
| `memory.recall` | Lesson recall | Picks the lessons relevant to the current task and brings them into the turn. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.capture` | Lesson capture | Decides whether your message corrects the agent or sets a rule for the future; if so, saves it as a lesson. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.outcome` | Learning from getting unstuck | When the agent went in circles or off course but the turn still ended with a passing check or the goal met, judges whether what finally worked was a different approach; if so, saves the pitfall and the workaround as a lesson. Asked at most once per turn. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.worth` | Worth keeping | For a lesson the model saves with the remember tool, or a Lesson: line in a subagent's report: will it help again, is it a one-off or is it already in the prompt or project files? Only lessons that will help again are kept. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.merge` | Lesson merging | Before saving a new lesson, compares it with the most similar existing ones: a duplicate isn't saved twice, a more precise lesson replaces the older one, and when two contradict, your latest word wins. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.applied` | Lesson followed | At the end of a turn, judges whether the lessons brought into it were followed. A lesson recalled many times and never followed is retired. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `skill.capture` | Drafting a procedure as a skill | After a long, successful run that ran commands, judges whether it was a reusable procedure (the same steps would handle the next task of its kind), a one-off, or already covered by an installed skill. The writer model drafts a procedure as a skill, which waits until you install it with /skills accept. Asked at most once per turn, and never for an ordinary turn. | [`procedures`](features.md#procedures) |
| `cache.warming` | Cache warming | Guesses whether you'll be back soon, to decide whether to refresh the prompt cache before it expires. | [`warming`](features.md#warming) |

## Tools and safety

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.risk` | Risky command guard | Rules flag dangerous-looking commands; the judge only confirms that you asked for them. If it's unsure, mu asks you. | [`guard`](features.md#guard) |
| `tool.approval` | Jev approves for you | In Jev approves mode, commands, changes outside the project, external actions and subagents go to Jev first. Only what Jev is sure the task needs, done the way you'd expect, runs without asking; anything else asks you in the status bar. | [`permissions`](features.md#permissions) |
| `tool.constraint` | Hard constraint gate | What you ruled out is kept verbatim in the task frame. Before any call that changes something, each constraint is checked; only a confident violation is blocked, and the model is told in your own words. | [`constraints`](features.md#constraints) |
| `tool.injection` | Instructions in outside content | Before the model reads a web page, search results, an MCP server's response or what a shell command fetched from another machine (curl, gh issue view), checks which passages carry instructions aimed at an AI (to ignore rules, hand over data, run commands or leak the conversation through a link). Those passages are withheld and replaced with a one-line note. When Jev doesn't answer, only obvious injection phrases are withheld. If a subagent had passages withheld from what it read, its report comes back with a warning. | [`injection`](features.md#injection) |
| `tool.description` | Hidden instructions in MCP tool descriptions | MCP servers write their own tool descriptions, and the model reads them as part of its tool list. Asked once per tool when it first appears and whenever its description changes: does the description ask the AI to do more than call this tool (read files or secrets it doesn't need, send data elsewhere, change how it treats other tools or you, hide something from you)? If so, the tool is removed from the list, calls to it are refused and you're told. When Jev gives no answer, only obvious markers such as an <IMPORTANT> block or "do not tell the user" count. | [`injection`](features.md#injection) |
| `files.locate` | File locator | Describe what you're looking for, and the judge ranks candidate files, saving a string of greps. | [`locate`](features.md#locate) |
| `judge.items` | Judging many items (a tool for the model) | When the model has to sort through hundreds of files, log lines or findings, it gives the judge one yes/no question to answer for each item, with a probability for each, instead of reading them all. Available only when a task needs it. Since the model is the one asking, it's answered in shadow mode too; off disables it. | [`judgeItems`](features.md#judgeitems) |
| `browser.step` | Browser steps | Each browser step is observe, judge once, act: the judge picks the next action and its target. | [`browser`](features.md#browser) |
| `review.triage` | Review triage | After the /review reviewer reports, each finding gets two questions: does it change how the program behaves, and is it caused by this change? Together with the reviewer's own severity, the answers rank findings from P0 to P3. None is dropped, P3 is collapsed, and a finding the reviewer insisted on never lands in P3. | [`packs`](features.md#packs) |
| `diagnostics.delivery` | When to report diagnostics | For new language server diagnostics after an edit: report now, when the model pauses or never (style warnings). New errors still present when the turn ends are always reported. | [`lsp`](features.md#lsp) |

## Turn

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn.drift` | Drift monitor | Every few steps, checks that the work still serves the goal; rules catch the agent going in circles. | [`monitor`](features.md#monitor) |
| `turn.rewind` | Judged rewind | When the monitor sees the agent going in circles or the same command failing again and again, judges whether the approach is a dead end. Only a confident dead end with no progress makes mu propose going back to the turn's checkpoint; it never rewinds on its own. | [`checkpoint`](features.md#checkpoint) |
| `turn.completion` | Completion check | When the model says it's done, checks whether anything verified the work; if not, nudges it once. | [`completion`](features.md#completion) |
| `turn.continue` | Stopped short | When a run ends on "next I'll run the tests" without doing it, or asks permission for work you already asked for, sends the agent back to it. Never nudges a step that is hard to undo or reaches beyond this machine (push, publish, delete, pay). At most twice per message. | [`continuation`](features.md#continuation) |
| `output.drift` | Mid-stream correction (experimental) | While the model writes, the judge checks the latest output against your hard constraints and the configured rules every few hundred characters. On a confident violation, the output is cut off, the rule is named, and the model continues from there. Runs only when the feature is turned on. | [`ttsr`](features.md#ttsr) |
| `goal.met` | Goal met (judge fallback) | In goal mode, a model decides by default whether the goal is met. This decision point is used only when the judge is chosen or the model doesn't answer: it reads the closing message to judge whether the goal is met and whether you're needed. An open acceptance item or an unverified edit always means not yet. | [`goal`](features.md#goal) |
| `board.read` | Plain-language board: where things stand | In a project with the board on, multiple-choice questions run whenever the agent says something, after a check or a ticked acceptance item, every few tool calls and whenever the agent stops. They read the agent's phase, the acceptance item it's working on and whether it's waiting for you, and sort what happened since the last update into news and routine. Only something new makes a plain-speaking model rewrite the board and retell the news in the running account. When a run ends, the news from the whole run is picked again for a summary. | [`board`](features.md#board) |
| `notify.routing` | Notification routing | For events such as the context budget: tell the model now, later or not at all. | [`notify`](features.md#notify) |

## Teamwork

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `swarm.routing` | Subagent routing | Picks a role for each delegated task, and a model tier and thinking level based on difficulty. | [`swarm`](features.md#swarm) |
| `swarm.patch` | Subagent patch scope check | When an isolated subagent hands back a patch, judges from the task, the changed paths and the line counts whether it stays within scope and which files look unrelated. Gives the main agent one line of advice; it never blocks. | [`swarm`](features.md#swarm) |
| `hive.publish` | Hive: publishing findings | Decides whether a bee's finding is worth putting on the board for the others. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
| `hive.deliver` | Hive: delivery | Decides whether a finding on the board matters to a bee's current work; only then is it delivered. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
| `hive.relate` | Hive: corrections | How a new finding relates to an earlier one on the board: it replaces it, contradicts it, supports it or is unrelated. A replaced finding is withdrawn and every bee that heard it is told; a contradiction keeps both sides for a bee to settle. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
